full_judgment: 130. From the side of the defence, they referred the case of Muhammad Siddiq Vs. The Crown, 6 DLR 56, where it has been held that where circumstances are enough to give rise to reasonable possibility that the defence plea might be true-Accused entitled to acquittal. The case of Safdar Ali-Vs.-The Crown, V DLR (FC) 64 where it has been held that special defence plea u/s 105 of the Evidence Act does not relieve the prosecution from proving its case beyond reasonable doubt. In a criminal case it is the duty of the Court to review the entire evidence that has been produced by the prosecution and the defence. If after an examination of the whole evidence, the Court is of the opinion that there is a reasonable possibility that the defence put forwarded by reacts on the whole prosecution case, in these circumstances, the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt, not as a matter of grace, but as of right, because the prosecution has not proved the case beyond reasonable doubt. The case of Alkas Mia and others-Vs.-The State, 25 DLR 398 where it has been held that non-examination of independent witnesses, particularly some of the neighbours, raises a presumption against the prosecution to the effect that had they been examined, they would not have supported the prosecution case. The case of Abdul Aziz-Vs. Sekander Ali and others, reported in 50 DLR 111, where it has been held that “দুটি খুনের জন্য আসামীদের বিরুদ্ধে একটি চার্জ গঠন করা হয়েছে । ইহা আইনসংগত হয় নাই। দুটি হত্যার জন্য পৃথক পৃথক ভাবে চার্জ গঠন করতে হবে।
